Yes, a lot about glass is fake. Till you make it. What I hear when you say what [OpenLight] is makes sense in many ways. The means, of course, that the engine is exposed to the internet. But what can be run what can be committed. Well, it's nice to expose something, but obviously there's a limit to what you can do. So we need a level of authentication or there needs to be scope to what you can commit. Really. Or the alternative is that the alternative for a website is that it connects to the storage and then runs its own engine in the client, right? So either you're able to download this and run it in the app, okay, that's how you get to touch a real engine where you can manipulate and do what you want, because then you have data ownership. But the site's just cloning the data. I don't know quite yet. What we're doing.

Yes. We are doing running an engine in the client. Of data in the client, and you can mutate it, in the browser. I mean, WYSIWYG, you can go ahead and tweak the UI and you know what you want. But there's a difference in once you restart the page, if it loads with data from the public storage or with the persisted data. I don't care for the engine locally yet. I don't. But this is not a fake it till we make it, so at least the store is correct. At least the interface is correct. For running locally, only the engine and the chassis would switch.
body.title: Where the engine runs
